title.official: Change in lawyer of record or self-representation

operative_text.controlling:
2.28(1)  A party may change the party’s lawyer of record or may
self-represent by
(a) serving a notice of the change in Form 3 on every other
party and on the lawyer or former lawyer of record, and
(b) filing an affidavit of service of the notice.
(2)  A self-represented litigant who retains a lawyer to act on the
litigant’s behalf must serve on every other party a notice to that
effect naming the lawyer of record.
(3)  The notice must include an address for service.
(4)  The notice is not required to be served on
(a) a party noted in default, or
(b) a party against whom default judgment has been entered.

BOOK_A.title: Change in Lawyer of Record or Self-representation
BOOK_A.related_provisions: 2.32 (lawyer ceasing to practice) ; 10.25 (records in lawyer’s possession) ; 11.17 (service on lawyer of record); 11.18 (service on self-represented person).
BOOK_A.commentary:
On need for a lawyer where the “client” is under a disability, see R.2.11n. , supra.
A party (or his trustee in bankruptcy stepping into his shoes) is always free to change solicitors,
or to start using a solicitor, and a contract with a solicitor cannot remove that right.¹
But if a change is done at the last moment, it may not be ground for an adjournment, and
the new solicitor may have to prepare in a very short time.²
However, if any substantial reason
for changing solicitors can be shown, the court will usually be fairly accommodating in giving
adjournments.³

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.554. Its subrule (1) was quite similar to 1914 R.563. Cf.1944 C. R.646, Ont. R.390, Judic. Ord. s.11, and 1883 O.7 r.2. Cf. Eng. O.67 r.1. 1968 R.554(2) was new in 1968. Came from Ont. R.391. Cf.1944 C. R.40, 1914 R.547, and Judic. Ord. r. 12. 1968 R.554(3) was new in 1968. Came from Ont. R.392. Cf.1944 C. R.40, 1914 R.547, and Judic. Ord. r. 12. 1968 R.554(7) was new in 1968. It came from the new B. C. Rule 44 d. Subrules (5) and (6) were new in 1968. The 1981 amendment to R.555 changed the name of a “notice of ceasing to act” to a “notice of withdrawal”.
See R.10.6(2). See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part F.

The costs otherwise payable to a successful plaintiff were signiﬁcantly reduced, because weeks before trial, that plaintiff’s counsel did not make herself known to opposing counsel, so there could be no pre-trial negotiation, or cooperation for trial: Morton v. Morton (#2) 2007 ABQB 345, affd 2008 ABCA 144.
See further the C. P. E. , Chapter 38, Part H.3.
